files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: N. Vartanian. Complete these in sequence; no skipping ahead.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; note that in some months every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and underlying contracts. Check the GL first to avoid a duplicate posting. If it has not been booked, record June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after first verifying what is already in the GL.
5. Match the June vendor bills to the GL expense coding. Verify each bill is in the correct expense account and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after all entries and reclasses from items 1-5 have been posted.
files.notes/company_background.md:
## Company background

Cascade Supply Partners began when two former regional distribution managers decided that smaller organizations deserved the same dependable sourcing support as national accounts. They built the business around a straightforward promise: answer the phone, know the products, and tell customers early when a shipment or substitute needs attention.

The company wholesales everyday workplace, shipping, packaging, breakroom, and light facility supplies to a mix of local and regional customers. Its team is deliberately compact. Account managers tend to know customers by voice, warehouse staff keep handwritten notes about recurring preferences, and the purchasing group has a reputation for finding practical alternatives when standard items are tight. The office culture is friendly but unsentimental; people help one another, then document what happened so the next order goes more smoothly.

Today, Cascade Supply Partners is an ordinary going concern focused on steady service and disciplined operations. The team is completing the June close while managing routine customer orders, vendor relationships, and fulfillment work. Leadership is also tightening expense coding, refreshing marketing materials, and reviewing internal processes that grew informally with the business. The aim is not reinvention, but a cleaner operating rhythm: reliable inventory decisions, clearer handoffs, timely accounting, and the personal service customers have come to expect.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction
Position Cascade Supply Partners as the responsive wholesale partner for teams that value dependable sourcing, practical substitutions, and a person who actually answers.

## Priorities
- Refresh the core brand language without losing the straightforward, local feel.
- Publish customer-friendly guidance on packaging, workplace supply planning, and avoiding fulfillment delays.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, led jointly by sales and purchasing.
- Pilot a partner co-marketing program with selected vendors.
- Give account managers reusable follow-up notes, product spotlights, and customer stories.

## Quarterly emphasis

### Q3
Complete messaging and visual cleanup. Build the webinar format, prepare the first topic series, and identify vendor partners willing to contribute useful expertise rather than sales pitches. Test a simple re-engagement campaign for quiet accounts.

### Q4
Expand the strongest Q3 content into sales tools and short customer emails. Continue the webinar cadence, publish the partner pilot results, and develop seasonal planning materials for customers with recurring supply needs.

## Working principles
Keep the voice practical, warm, and specific. Avoid inflated claims. Marketing should make the sales conversation easier, not louder.

## Measurement
Track attendance quality, account-manager follow-up, customer replies, partner participation, and sales conversations influenced by each activity. Final resourcing remains subject to the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from your chatty predecessor

N. Vartanian — a few things I learned the hard way:

- The bank slips its own fees and charges in near the end of the statement. Those are booked during close, not as the month rolls along, so do not assume the ledger already has them.
- June moved fast, and some vendor-bill expense coding may be off. Compare the GL with the source documents and treat the files in bills/ as authoritative.
- The budget was locked early in Q2. The one-off June work was never included, which is why it should explain most of the larger budget-to-actual variances.
- This month, the June 16-30 payroll run pays in the first days of July. The payroll register has the support, so make sure the timing is reflected in the close.

That is the short version. Start with the source documents and the reconciliations; they will keep you out of trouble.
